_readme: TEMPLATE — copy this file, rename it, fill it in. One file = one vlog.
Files starting with _ are ignored by the loader, so this one never renders.
Name the copy after the vlog, e.g. first-light-to-nathakadaiyur.json — the
filename becomes the id (and the URL segment) when `id` is left out.
ORDER: OLDEST FIRST, by `created` — the list reads as a journey, so the
garage section's road starts at the first vlog and the stop numbers count
up from it. Set `created` when you add the file and never touch it again —
that is what fixes the order. `date` is when the video was actually filmed
and is what the page displays; if `created` is missing the loader falls
back to `date`, then to the filename.
REQUIRED: nothing but a title. A file in this folder IS a page — it shows
up in the garage section and gets its own /mygarage/vlogs/<filename> page
as soon as it exists. Every field is optional and each one just fills in
more of that page: drop `description` and the write-up section disappears,
drop `images` and the frame-grab strip does, and so on.
NO VIDEO YET? Leave `video` empty. The page and the card still appear and
say the video is still to come, so a ride can be written up and routed
before the cut is uploaded. Paste the link later and the player appears.
THERE IS NO FIELD FOR 'UP NEXT'. That section is built from the OTHER
files in this folder — same category first, newest first within each group
(it is a what-to-watch list, so it runs the opposite way to the road).
Add a second vlog and each one starts pointing at the other. Same for the
garage section's list and its counters: all of it is this folder.
PATHS: images and clips are paths inside public/ — put vlog photos in
public/mygarage/vlog/images/ and reference them as
'mygarage/vlog/images/<file>'. Absolute https:// URLs are left alone.
`videos` is extra clips belonging to THIS vlog, shown after the images —
a second angle, a cut that missed the main edit. Not to be confused with
`video` (the vlog itself) or Up Next (the other files in this folder).
A bare YouTube link is enough; an object adds a title, caption or
duration; and a local .mp4/.webm/.mov in public/ works as well.
See src/data/vlogs.js for the full field-by-field reference.
title: The vlog title
subtitle: The line that sits under the title
excerpt: One or two sentences. Used on cards and as the standfirst.
description: A plain string is a paragraph. The first one gets the drop cap.
_instagram_note: A bare /p/ or /reel/ link is enough — those embed themselves.
A STORY or HIGHLIGHT link (instagram.com/s/...) cannot embed: Instagram
serves no embed for those. It still appears, as a card that opens the
story on Instagram — but give it a `poster` (a screenshot you saved) and
the print shows that picture instead, which is far better. Keep the
